12	---
13	write a script that will:
14	
15	* create a new tag on github with the current release number as can be read in [package.json](desktop/package.json)
16	* use that tag to create a new release on github. 
17	  * use the version as the release title
18	  * for the release notes, use the release\_notes.md files saved in the latest release folder, a sub folder of  `design\releases`. This folder will have as name, the current release number where the '.' are replaced with '\_'
19	  * upload the latest build found in `{{repository-folder}}/release`.  filename will be MD2-Setup-{{version}}-x64 where {{version}} is the release version.
20	* publish that release
21	
22	## Current state
23	
24	- Version source: `desktop/package.json` `version` (now `0.8.3`). `scripts/update_version.ps1` sets it in `app/` and `desktop/` `package.json`. `desktop/packaging/BUILDING_WINDOWS.md` names `desktop/package.json` authoritative.

26	- Release notes: complete-release flow (`app/src/services/release_operations.ts`) moves cards into `design/releases/<release name>`; folder name is release name typed by user. Latest folder `design/releases/0.8.3` uses dots, so script uses version unchanged as folder name (user decision; spec text about `_` is superseded). Older folders use `_` (`0_7_0`); `0.8.0` has no `release_notes.md`.
27	- `release_notes.md` starts with frontmatter (`---` block holding `internalId`), then `# MD² <version>` and bullets. Frontmatter is md2 metadata, not release text.
28	- Existing git tags use `V_0_7_1` style. New script uses `v<version>` (user decision), e.g. `v0.8.3`. Old tags untouched.
29	- No GitHub release tooling in repository: no `.github/workflows`, no release script. `gh` (GitHub CLI) not installed on this machine. Remote `origin` = `https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2.git`.
30	- Script precedent: `scripts/update_version.ps1` (PowerShell 5.1, `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`, `throw` on invalid input) with plain-PowerShell test `scripts/update_version.test.ps1`.
31	
32	## Implementation details
33	
34	New file `scripts/publish_release.ps1`. Runs from any working directory; resolves repository root via `Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot`. No parameters: version always read from `desktop/package.json`.
35	
36	Prerequisite (document in script header comment): `gh` installed and authenticated (`gh auth login`) with push and release rights on `origin`.
37	
38	Steps, in order. Every validation runs before first remote change, so failed validation changes nothing on GitHub:
39	
40	1. Read `desktop/package.json` (UTF-8), parse with `ConvertFrom-Json`, take `version`. Missing or non-string: `throw`.
41	2. Derive values once: `$tag = "v$version"`, release title = `$version`, notes path = `design/releases/$version/release_notes.md`, installer path = `release/MD2-Setup-$version-x64.exe`.
42	3. Validate:
43	   - `gh` available (`Get-Command gh`); else `throw` with install hint.
44	   - Notes file exists; else `throw` naming expected path.
45	   - Installer file exists; else `throw` naming expected path. Script never builds.
46	   - Tag absent locally (`git tag --list $tag`) and on `origin` (`git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/$tag`); else `throw` "Tag already exists". Prevents re-publishing same version.
47	4. Notes text: read notes file, strip leading frontmatter block (first line `---` up to next `---` line), trim. Empty result: `throw`. Write text to temporary file (`[System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName()`, UTF-8 without BOM); delete it in `finally`.
48	5. Create annotated tag on current `HEAD`: `git tag -a $tag -m "MD² $version"`. Push: `git push origin $tag`. HEAD means commit currently checked out; user is responsible for checking out release commit.
49	6. Create draft release with asset: `gh release create $tag $installerPath --title $version --notes-file $notesFile --verify-tag --draft`. `--verify-tag` makes `gh` fail instead of silently creating tag on GitHub. Draft keeps release hidden until upload finished.
50	7. Publish: `gh release edit $tag --draft=false`.
51	8. After each `git`/`gh` call check `$LASTEXITCODE`; non-zero: `throw` with command and step. Native commands do not trigger `$ErrorActionPreference`.
52	9. Output release URL (`gh release view $tag --json url --jq .url`).
53	
54	Failure modes:
55	- Failure after tag push (step 6 or 7): tag and maybe draft stay on GitHub. Script does not roll back; error message lists cleanup: `gh release delete $tag --cleanup-tag` and `git tag -d $tag`. Rationale: rollback of remote state adds complexity for rare case.
56	- Only `.exe` uploaded; `.blockmap` excluded (spec names only installer; no auto-update consumes blockmap).
57	
58	New test `scripts/publish_release.test.ps1`, same style as `scripts/update_version.test.ps1`. Fixture temp folder holds copied script, `desktop/package.json`, notes file, dummy installer. Test defines PowerShell functions `git` and `gh` before invoking script; functions take precedence over executables, so calls are recorded, nothing external runs. Stubs set `$global:LASTEXITCODE`.
59	
60	Out of scope (not requested): action JSON in `design/actions` to run script from md2, building installer, CI workflow, renaming old tags or folders.
61	
62	## Acceptance criteria
63	
64	- Running `powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/publish_release.ps1` with version `0.8.3`, existing `design/releases/0.8.3/release_notes.md` and `release/MD2-Setup-0.8.3-x64.exe`:
65	  - creates and pushes annotated tag `v0.8.3` on `HEAD`;
66	  - creates published (non-draft) GitHub release for `v0.8.3` titled `0.8.3`;
67	  - release body equals `release_notes.md` content without frontmatter;
68	  - release has one asset `MD2-Setup-0.8.3-x64.exe`;
69	  - prints release URL.
70	- Missing notes file, missing installer, missing `gh`, or existing tag (local or `origin`): script exits non-zero with message naming cause; no tag created, nothing pushed, no `gh release` call.
71	- Failing `git`/`gh` call stops script with non-zero exit; message names failed step; after tag push, message includes cleanup commands.
72	- Temporary notes file removed on success and failure.
73	- `scripts/publish_release.test.ps1` covers: happy path (recorded `git`/`gh` arguments in order, notes without frontmatter), each validation failure (no remote-changing call recorded), non-zero exit from stubbed `gh release create`. Runs without network, git, or `gh`.

I've added the three sections to `design/feature_descriptions/F_417_after_action_select_focus_input_box.md` and set `status: ready for implementation`. Nothing is staged or committed, and no code was changed.

**Your answers, as written into the doc:**
- The rule fires when the user clicks an action in the action selector, and also when the popup opens with its first action.
- Command actions count too: their "Run" button is treated like "Send".
- If the input has text but the Send/Run button is disabled or hidden, the input box gets focus instead.

**Design in brief:**
- **One-time focus request.** Each time an action is picked, the popup builds a fresh set of per-action state. A small new class, `ActionPopupFocusRequest`, joins that state as a flag that can be used once. Updates to the same action (for example a context change during a run) don't move focus again.
- **Who decides.** `ActionPopupRunControls` makes the choice, because it already knows whether the input is empty, whether its text is still loading, and whether the button is visible and enabled.
- **Waiting for text.** For agent actions, the default input text is loaded from the backend after selection. Focus is applied only once that text has arrived, and nothing is focused if loading fails.
- **Focusing the input box.** This uses a new focus-request event on `MarkdownDraft`, the same way flush and insertion requests already work. `useMarkdownDraft` passes it to the editor, which focuses itself in plain-text, rich, or source mode.
- **Timing.** The focus runs in a `useEffect`, not a layout effect, so it happens after the popup frame grabs focus when it first opens.
- **Tests** are listed for the popup, the draft hook and the new class.

**Things to check:**
- On mobile, focusing the input on open will pop up the on-screen keyboard. The doc keeps the same rule there.
- If loading the default text is slow or waits for a reconnect, focus can move noticeably later than the click.
- I marked as out of scope: focus after picking a conversation, and focus after a run completes.
